title: All That Glisters Is Softmax: Shiny-Object Interns, Airplane-Magazine Execs, and Why AI Labs Can Only Bake In Half the Scars
why_read: A rambling, metaphor-heavy opinion piece with little concrete technical content beneath the flowery language.
analysis: This article uses extended literary and cultural metaphors (Shakespeare, airplane magazines, power loaders) to make points about AI coding workflows and model limitations, but it buries any actual technical claims under dense rhetorical style. It's unclear what concrete, falsifiable claim or technique the piece is actually presenting about language models or production AI systems. It reads more as a stylistic essay than a substantive technical piece, so it offers little practical value to engineers looking for clear information.
